title.en: Objectives and limitations of financial analysis

heading.en: Why analyse, and what can go wrong?

hook.en: A doctor reads a blood report to diagnose and to plan treatment, but knows a single test can mislead. *Financial analysis* works the same way.
hook.kn: ವೈದ್ಯರು ರಕ್ತ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯ ವರದಿಯಿಂದ ರೋಗ ಪತ್ತೆ ಮಾಡಿ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಯೋಜಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ, ಆದರೆ ಒಂದೇ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ತಪ್ಪುದಾರಿಗೆಳೆಯಬಹುದು ಎಂದೂ ತಿಳಿದಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಹಣಕಾಸು ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಣೆಯೂ ಹಾಗೆಯೇ.

say.en: A doctor reads a blood report to diagnose and to plan treatment, but knows a single test can mislead. Financial analysis works the same way. In this lesson: State the objectives of analysis.
Explain the limitations of analysis.

body.en: To assess the current profitability and operational efficiency; to ascertain the relative importance of different components of the *financial* position; to identify reasons for changes in profitability and position; to judge the ability to repay interest and principal (solvency); to assess short-term liquidity; to compare with other firms and the industry; and to forecast.
body.kn: ಲಾಭದಾಯಕತೆ, ದಕ್ಷತೆ, ದ್ರವ್ಯತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಋಣ ತೀರಿಕೆ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ ತಿಳಿಯಲು, ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯ ಕಾರಣ ಅರಿಯಲು, ಹೋಲಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಮುನ್ಸೂಚನೆಗಾಗಿ ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ.

text.en: Analysis is a means, not an end

say.en: Bought one hundred units at ten rupees, then one hundred at twelve. Sold one hundred for fifteen hundred.

prompt.en: Sort each statement about financial analysis.

text.en: To judge current profitability and efficiency
To find the reasons for changes in profit
To judge the ability to repay loans and interest
To compare the firm with others in its industry
It ignores changes in the price level
It ignores qualitative factors such as staff morale

explanation.en: Analysis aims to judge profitability, position, repaying capacity and trends; it is limited because it inherits the limits of the statements: historical cost, no price-level changes, no qualitative factors, and differences in policy.

say.en: Objective or limitation? Sort each statement about financial analysis.

body.en: *Analysis* is only as good as the statements: it inherits their historical nature and ignores price-level changes. Qualitative aspects are ignored. Window dressing and different accounting policies distort comparisons. Analysis is a means, not an end; it needs the judgement of an expert.
body.kn: ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಣೆ ಹಣಕಾಸು ತಃಖ್ತೆಗಳ ಮಿತಿಗಳನ್ನೇ ಹೊಂದಿರುತ್ತದೆ: ಐತಿಹಾಸಿಕ ಅಂಕಿಗಳು, ಹಣದುಬ್ಬರ ಕಡೆಗಣನೆ, ಗುಣಾತ್ಮಕ ಅಂಶಗಳ ಕೊರತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕಿಟಕಿ ಅಲಂಕಾರದ ಅಪಾಯ.

problem.en: Firm X values inventory by FIFO and Firm Y by weighted average. Prices rose steadily during the year. Each has identical physical sales and purchases. Which firm reports higher profit, and why is comparison risky?

steps.en: With rising prices, FIFO leaves the latest (higher) prices in closing inventory.
Higher closing inventory means lower cost of goods sold, so Firm X shows a higher profit.
The difference comes from accounting policy, not performance, so inter-firm comparison can mislead.

answer.en: Firm X reports higher profit; differing accounting policies limit comparison.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Firm X values inventory by FIFO and Firm Y by weighted average. Prices rose steadily during the year. Each has identical physical sales and purchases. Which firm reports higher profit, and why is comparison risky?
With rising prices, FIFO leaves the latest higher prices in closing inventory.
Higher closing inventory means lower cost of goods sold, so Firm X shows a higher profit.
The difference comes from accounting policy, not performance, so inter-firm comparison can mislead.
So the answer is Firm X reports higher profit; differing accounting policies limit comparison.
